reviewContext.openQuestion: Is behavioral-spec.md's 'registry.json live slots only' scope-narrowing (post iteration-5 FIND-001/FIND-002) a defensible boundary, or does it leave a real wallet-misresolution vector open?

scopeDecisionReasoning: The scope CRITERION itself (in-scope iff a file is the literal entrypoint of a registry.json live slot, because only that dispatch path can ever hand a script a different caller's ANICCA_HOME) is sound in principle. But its APPLICATION in the 'closed audit' table is not exhaustive: it checked only each live slot's entrypoint file's own inline content, not what that entrypoint execs into. `earn/clip-producer` is a live registry slot whose entrypoint (run.sh) execs into skills/earn/clip/producer.sh, which still contains the byte-identical unfixed vulnerable preamble, inside the SAME per-instance-dispatched process. This one file was mischaracterized as clean. For the other 3 files iteration 5 flagged (clip-promote/run.sh, x402-sell/serve-mainnet-boot.sh, clip-producer.plist), the out-of-scope classification IS independently correct and defensible: none is registry.json-dispatched, and none depends on ANICCA_HOME for wallet/key resolution in its actual current code path.

flaggedFiles.reasoning: Not a registry.json slot (absent from skills/registry.json's slot list; header comment's claim of being a 'run-skill.mjs SLOT entrypoint' is not reflected in the registry) -- never dispatched via index.mjs's per-instance buildSkillEnv/spawn(). Line 19's `set -a; . "$HOME/.openclaw/.env"...; set +a` does clobber this script's OWN ANICCA_HOME, but zero code in this file or its subprocesses (record-payout.mjs invoked under `env -i` with an explicit var allowlist at lines 56-59 that excludes ANICCA_HOME; WALLET defaults to a hardcoded Solana address at line 25) ever reads ANICCA_HOME. Grep confirms zero ANICCA_HOME references in the whole clip-promote directory. Out-of-scope classification is DEFENSIBLE for wallet-misresolution purposes; the vulnerable string remains as pure repo-hygiene debt.

registry.json's `x402_sell` slot's real `dir` is `skills/earn` (the EARN_ALLOW-allowlisted legacy fat slot), NOT `skills/earn/x402-sell` -- this file is a genuinely separate, non-registry-dispatched standalone KeepAlive launchd daemon. serve.mjs's payTo() (skills/earn/x402-sell/serve.mjs:31-38) only calls the ANICCA_HOME-dependent loadEvmKey() when process.env.X402_PAYTO is unset, but serve-mainnet-boot.sh hardcodes X402_PAYTO='0x810f6d61f7606deee2657d3083e150a222bc29c5' at line 11 BEFORE exec'ing serve.mjs -- the ANICCA_HOME-dependent branch is provably dead code in this script's actual invocation. Out-of-scope classification is DEFENSIBLE.

Currently NOT wallet-misresolving (zero ANICCA_HOME references anywhere in skills/earn/clip/, confirmed by directory-wide grep) -- but this is the one file whose out-of-scope reclassification is NOT DEFENSIBLE, because it is directly reachable, via `exec` (same-process, not a subshell), from registry.json's LIVE `earn/clip-producer` slot (skills/earn/clip-producer/run.sh:19: `exec bash '.../clip/producer.sh' "$@"`) -- the exact per-instance-dispatched path REQ-004's own criterion defines as in-scope. behavioral-spec.md's audit table (line 171) incorrectly marks this slot as having no vulnerable pattern. Per REQ-003's own precedent (fix dormant instances in live-dispatched paths, do not leave latent), this file must receive the shared-helper fix regardless of today's dormancy -- see FIND-001.

A standalone launchd job (own Label/StartCalendarInterval/log paths) that execs producer.sh directly; launchd starts it with no caller ANICCA_HOME to preserve in the first place, and it is not registry.json-dispatched. Out-of-scope classification is independently DEFENSIBLE for this .plist itself. It shares the same downstream producer.sh dependency as the finding above, so fixing producer.sh centrally (required regardless, per FIND-001) resolves this file's residual exposure for free.

requiredFixList: skills/earn/clip/producer.sh -- route its env-loading preamble (currently line 22) through skills/_shared/lib/load-instance-env.sh, identically to the 4 already-fixed call sites. This is a mechanical extension of the existing REQ-004 fix, not new design.

Correct behavioral-spec.md's audit-table row for earn/clip-producer (currently line 171, 'no'/'Not applicable — clean') to reflect that it transitively contains (and, after the fix, delegates) the vulnerable pattern via its exec into clip/producer.sh.

Add a note to REQ-004's scope criterion that 'literal entrypoint of a live registry.json slot' must include tracing exec-chains from that entrypoint, not just the entrypoint file's own inline content -- otherwise the same class of miss can recur for any other slot with a thin exec-wrapper entrypoint.
